                data[key].setdefault(row[1][:7],[]).append(float(row[2]))
            except: pass
months=sorted({m for d in data.values() for m in d})
print('Zone_F3_Z01 setpoints vs F2_Z01 setpoints:')
for m in months:
    z33c=data['5b98cbc1-fd25-5d8c-a96e-c3de49819174'].get(m)
    z33h=data['b7f22e0c-833d-5373-87e1-51e1cb26f038'].get(m)

    z21h=data['b5c23ef3-f09b-5290-bfe0-1017cde1c4a5'].get(m)
    f=lambda v: round(sum(v)/len(v),2) if v else None
    print(m,'F3Z01 cool=',f(z33c),'heat=',f(z33h),' F2Z01 cool=',f(z21c),'heat=',f(z21h))

content.text: The data show Zone_F3_Z01's reported temperature starts diverging from its F3 peers around July 2018: while F3_Z02, F3_Z03, F3_Z05 still track the normal seasonal curve (up in summer, down to ~22 °C in winter by Dec 2018 / Jan 2019), Zone_F3_Z01 stays pinned around 25 °C year-round and even climbs to 26.37 °C in Jan 2019. Setpoints are identical across zones, and other zones are not affected — this isolated, flat-then-rising trace is the classic signature of a single zone sensor drifting, not a real local load change (which would also show in the cooling/heating setpoint/command or in the shared air path).
